text: The rwb-case case state and move answer, the rwb-partner buyer organisation read, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-decision package are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-case writes recovery_case and the route states, only rwb-partner owns partner and partner_user, only rwb-access owns the rights and only rwb-decision governs the rule rows, and TSD S6 T5.2 names the cross-module interfaces without publishing an operation name. The plan's C row for the slice is empty, so the rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata.

why: Architecture v5 gives rwb-debtsale two events, LotAwarded and AccountsTransferred, with consumers rwb-case and rwb-reporting, and the source precedence puts the Arch v5 catalogue slides above the TSD, which lists LotAwarded alone. DP-09 and DP-14 are not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, so adding the library to the metadata would invent a dependency value.

text: The buyer file is delivered by rwb-integration's deliverFile activity on queue rwb-integration, per lot under INT-25, encrypted and through the data room; this service instructs the delivery and keeps its reference, and builds no transport, holds no key and writes no shared directory. RWB-P2-E1007-CON is a tracked dependency and not a metadata row.
why: Architecture v5 gives rwb-debtsale 'Integration: deliverFile (buyer file)', the connection matrix gives S6 a Temporal call to P2, and TSD S6 T5.1 keeps INT-25 as an outbound file per lot through the data room. DP-16 is absent from the pattern set of this key and the plan's C row is empty, so the row cannot be added without inventing a metadata value.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-16 and R5.4 class C; TSD S6 T5.1; Architecture v5 slide 8 (debt buyers, encrypted files) and OUT row of rwb-debtsale; context pack connection-matrix row S6

text: The transfer is recorded as the lot status TRANSFERRED on debt_sale_lot, one decision record carrying the delivery reference and the transfer time, and the AccountsTransferred event; no transfer column is added to debt_sale_account.
why: The legacy story says the transfer is recorded and TSD S6 T3.1 publishes no transfer time, no file reference and no transfer status on debt_sale_account, while the only writable state that expresses the transfer is the lot status of LOV-LOT-STATUS. Adding a column would be a schema change no source authorises and no DB story of this slice holds.

text: The settled fact arrives as the release signal of the settlement step of DebtSaleWorkflow, whose ProceedsMatched consumer group and inbox row are RWB-S6-E6011-APP's; this story confirms the settlement under R-DS-25 for the release it owns and holds no subscription of its own, and the rule is evaluated once per case on the same fact.

text: The five-working-day target of R-DS-29, the settlement condition of R-DS-25 and the 45-day turnaround are read as rule and reference values with their version, and none is a timer constant, a schema default or a branch of the build.
why: R-DS-29 carries the timer '5 working days', R-DS-25 the condition 'payment received in full', and FSD S6 A2.11.1 the 45-day metric, while FSD S6 BR-S6-011 and the legacy guardrails forbid a value a business person may change being written in code. The values therefore belong to the package and the reference data, not to this build.

Restating the channel that fronts the buyer would add a plan row the sources do not give, so the channel is declared as a consumed path and recorded.
